The construction panels reveal real spatial thinking — ellipse axes, perspective bounding boxes, and center lines are all present and doing useful work.

⚠️ Where to Pivot: The critical weakness is the insufficient contrast between 'concept view' and 'presentation view' in the bottom row. A presentation view must feel decisively different from its construction counterpart — the viewer should immediately sense that all scaffolding has been resolved and hidden. In the bottom-right panel, residual construction lines and tentative strokes compete with the intended contour, collapsing the distinction the assignment is specifically designed to train. Additionally, the design itself reads as a direct transcription of a reference product rather than a student-authored form — even small proportional departures (a taller neck, a wider base, a more pronounced taper) would signal design authorship.

🛠️ Next Step: Take the bottom-right panel and redraw it as a standalone clean presentation view — but this time, physically cover your construction sketch before you begin. Work only from memory and spatial understanding, committing each line as a final contour without correction strokes. This exercise will force you to internalize the form well enough to draw it with conviction, and will train the decisive line quality that separates a presentation view from a working sketch.
